subject: Media Literacy
title: War on Terror and Media
description: A quick, practical guide to War on Terror and Media.

hook.text: Colin Powell held up a vial at the UN, claiming Iraq had weapons of mass destruction. They didn't.

buildup.text: After 9/11, media coverage was saturated with government messaging that justified military action.

discovery.text: Embedded journalism put reporters inside military units, providing access but limiting perspective.

twist.text: The phrase 'War on Terror' was itself propaganda — framing a complex issue as a simple binary.

climax.text: The Iraq War showed how media can amplify government claims without adequate fact-checking.

punchline.text: The evidence was thin. The headlines were thick.

quiz.question: What media issue did embedded journalism create?
options: It gave access but limited independent perspective
